clue.text: The moon's faint shimmering suits the bard's play

indicators.note: something shimmering wavers and shifts about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter: the word moon is used as written

explanation.surface: A Romantic image of pale moonlight that suits a play by Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shimmering' rearranges THEMOONFAINT plus the S of moon's; the bard is Shakespeare, and this is one of his lesser-known tragedies. 'suits' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare, called the Bard, wrote this tragedy about a misanthropic Greek nobleman.

clue.text: Very happy, yet shattered?

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed yet also exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: something shattered has been broken to bits, read as 'thrilled' into pieces. 'yet' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Very happy is the idiom's everyday sense of delight; shattered plays on the literal sense of being smashed into fragments.

clue.text: Some animal tamed in the country

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a particular country an animal has been tamed.
explanation.definitionFit: An island republic in the Mediterranean is a country.

clue.text: Not all knights had escaped something deadly?

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tale of only some knights escaping a fatal danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade is a poisonous plant, so it is a lethal thing.

clue.text: Tragically overweight partner

parts.note: overweight means fat
a partner is an ally

explanation.surface: Lament for an obese companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done tragically ends in death or disaster, a deadly outcome.

clue.text: Man with certain promises going on and on

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A man who keeps making promises and droning on.
explanation.walkthrough: IOU is short for 'I owe you', a written acknowledgement of debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boring drags, seeming to go on interminably.

clue.text: Lord beheaded king, then left

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the king's name is cut off

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A nobleman cut off a monarch's head and departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer ranked above a viscount is addressed as a lord.

clue.text: Feeling ecstatic, fellows engaged in children's game

parts.note: sent is slang for transported with delight

indicators.note: engaged in says the fellows are placed inside the game's name

parts.note: it is another name for tag, the chasing game
fellows are men

explanation.surface: An excited feeling as grown men join in a playground game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent' as 'ecstatic' is dated slang ('that music really sends me'); the playground chasing game tag is also called 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling is an emotion or attitude, a synonym of sentiment.

clue.text: I send clerk cash — ruined writer

indicators.note: ruined says the letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A clerk sending off cash has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges ISENDCLERKCASH; fittingly, the novelist wrote about clerks and debtors' ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian author of novels like Bleak House is a writer.

clue.text: For example, like family members kept outside and reduced in status

indicators.note: kept outside says the family-members word is kept around the example abbreviation

parts.note: family members are related

explanation.surface: Relatives shut out and demoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegated means demoted, moved down to a lower rank or division.

clue.text: Big farm extended beside church

parts.note: ran in the sense of stretched or extended, as a fence ran for miles

explanation.surface: A large farm stretching out next to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cattle farm, especially in America, is a ranch.

clue.text: Jumped in meadow, a form of training

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for meadow
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Someone bounding about in a field as part of their exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is a past tense of leap, to spring or bound.

clue.text: Country girl almost hiding love

indicators.note: hiding says the love letter is concealed inside the shortened girl
almost means the girl's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A country girl keeps her romance a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts LASS to LAS, and 'hiding' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked state in Southeast Asia is a country.

clue.text: Support that is keeping pair together

indicators.note: keeping says the pair abbreviation holds the that-is abbreviation inside

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation for that is (id est)

explanation.surface: Something that props up and keeps a couple together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'together' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar holding up a bridge or arch is a structural support.

clue.text: Nasty claims lodged by a French worker

indicators.note: lodged by says the claims are placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: un is French for a
an ant is a worker
pleas are claims made in court

explanation.surface: Unpleasant demands placed by a French labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a French' gives the French article, not the letter A; 'lodged by' signals the claims sitting inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nasty is disagreeable or offensive.

clue.text: Paintings by Henry in cathedral not divine

indicators.note: in says the paintings and Henry are placed inside the cathedral

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city
paintings are art
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Art and a portrait of Henry displayed in a cathedral, but nothing heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword stock answer for 'cathedral'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly means worldly, belonging to this world rather than heaven.

clue.text: Screens from the east with crimson flowers outside

indicators.note: outside says the flowers go around the other pieces

parts.note: roses are flowers
E is the abbreviation for east
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Screens in the east decorated with red flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'with' are links; 'from the east' looks like a reversal signal but simply gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Evil church about to become free of hypocrisy

parts.note: evil is sin
CE is the Church of England
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A wicked church about to reform and become honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sincere is genuine, not pretending to feelings they do not hold.

clue.text: Harangues one involved in deals

indicators.note: involved in says the numeral one is placed inside the deals

parts.note: trades are deals
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rant from someone mixed up in shady deals.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long angry speech, a rant.

clue.text: Guess everyone must tuck into an onion

indicators.note: tuck into says everyone is put inside the guess

parts.note: a shot is a guess, an attempt
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Guess what: everyone must eat an onion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must' is a link. 'tuck into' suggests eating, but it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mild bulb of the onion family is a shallot.

clue.text: Like certain piper ensnaring group to be led

indicators.note: ensnaring says the piper word traps the group inside it

parts.note: the Pied Piper of Hamelin, so pied describes a certain piper
a lot is a group, a batch

explanation.surface: A piper trapping a crowd that will follow him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to guide or steer, so piloted means led.

clue.text: Work for each group of pupils

parts.note: per means for each
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Homework set for every class.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORM is a British school class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that works is functioning, doing its job.

clue.text: Sign of new life shown by English seaside resort

parts.note: a bud is the first sign of new growth on a plant

explanation.surface: Spring signs of life at an English seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: BUDE is a seaside town in Cornwall, south-west England. 'shown by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bude is a Cornish coastal holiday town, a seaside resort.

clue.text: Hard expression bringing shock?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an air is an expression or look

explanation.surface: A stern look that causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like surprise, but a shock is a thick mass of hair; the question mark flags the trick. 'bringing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a bushy, untidy mass of locks on the head.

clue.text: Greek in a garret

explanation.surface: A Greek living up in a garret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means of Athens, so Greek; and a loft room under the roof is a garret.

clue.text: Piece of flesh ready to cook after short time

indicators.note: after says the cooking word follows the time abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
game meat is hung until it is high, gamey and ready to cook

explanation.surface: Meat that has been hung and is now ready to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Game is hung until high, slightly decomposed, before cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper leg is a fleshy part of the body or a joint of meat.

clue.text: Grumble when buzzer's loud

parts.note: a bee is a buzzer; the 's stands for is and adds no letter
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A complaint when the buzzer is noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang for a complaint, a gripe.

clue.text: Smack son going into gallery

indicators.note: going into says the son abbreviation enters the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A slap as a boy walks into an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a slap, but it means a flavour or trace, as in 'smacks of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a slight flavour, a taste.

clue.text: Cause of double vision

parts.note: seeing double is usually a medical complaint, but here it is a person who resembles another, so one seems to see the same face twice

explanation.surface: A medical question about what makes someone see double.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a person who looks exactly like another, so seeing one feels like seeing twice.

clue.text: They keep strikers away from dangerously inflammatory situations

definitions.text: They keep strikers away from dangerously inflammatory situations

parts.words: They keep strikers away from dangerously inflammatory situations
parts.note: the surface suggests riot police keeping industrial strikers away from trouble; the strikers are really little sticks that light only on a special surface on their box

explanation.surface: Officers keep pickets away from a volatile confrontation.
explanation.definitionFit: These matches ignite only on the box's prepared strip, reducing the risk of accidental fire.
